# nf-claw

> A self-maintaining, token-minimal library of nf-core Nextflow DSL2 pipelines curated for autonomous AI agents and bioinformaticians. Upstream source trees remain unmodified; execution includes documented, source-guarded runtime corrections alongside deterministic preflight validation, strict identifier hygiene, cryptographic provenance bundles, reproducible replay guards, and multi-stage pipeline chaining.

nf-claw provides AI agents with structured, machine-actionable instructions and CLI tooling to discover, configure, execute, and chain production-grade nf-core bioinformatic pipelines using pinned parameter references and a shared runner.

Key conventions for AI agents navigating this repository:
- Discover without token bloat: Do not read full catalogs or directory listings. Run `nfclaw list <keywords>` (ranked matches) or grep `catalog.json` (or `catalog.md`) for keywords.
- Inspect pipeline skills: Read `pipelines/<name>/skill.md` for required inputs, parameters, and schema-derived run commands. Consult `pipelines/<name>/reference.md` for complete parameter constraints.
- Run a pipeline: Execute with `nfclaw run <name> --input <file> --outdir <dir> -profile <profile>` (or `python3 -m runner run ...`). Use Python 3.11+; pass `--check` for explicit-value preflight and command inspection without launching pipeline tasks. It leaves the output directory untouched but can initialize sources and probe the engine.
- No samplesheet yet: pass the data files as `--input` (a directory, a quoted glob, or files with `--input` once each) and nfclaw generates the samplesheet from the pipeline's own schema; set the columns no file name determines with `--sheet-set COLUMN=VALUE` (listed under Inputs in each `skill.md`).
- Check status: Monitor foreground or background runs with `nfclaw status <outdir>`. Runs are logged to `<outdir>/provenance/logs/run.log` and protected by a non-blocking writer lock beside the output directory (`.<outdir name>.nfclaw.lock`).
- Sample identity safety: Scientific metadata identifiers (`meta.id`, sample/patient IDs, genome/database names) must start with a letter, digit or underscore and contain only letters, digits, combining marks, dots, underscores or hyphens (Unicode letters and digits count). nfclaw refuses other identifiers rather than renaming samples. Local paths in samplesheets must always be absolute.
- Multi-stage chaining: Orchestrate sequential pipelines via declarative JSON specs with `nfclaw chain run <spec.json> --outdir <dir>`.
- Replay & verification: Reproduce runs into fresh targets using `<outdir>/provenance/commands.sh` (new bundles archive tracked source, copy replayable configs and pin eligible container processes; the replay compares its recorded environment and fails detected mismatches, while unverified entries remain reported gaps) and verify results with `nfclaw verify <target> --against <original>`.
- Scientific output assessment: Check declared scientific outputs, parsed formats (BAM, VCF, FASTA, TSV, H5AD), sample coverage and rational numeric tolerances against contracts with `nfclaw assess <outdir> --contract <file> [--against <original>]`.
- MCP: `nfclaw mcp` serves the library and runner to MCP clients (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Hermes) on stdio; runs and chains become detached jobs followed by job id (`docs/mcp.md`).
- Operational manual: Read `AGENTS.md` before executing or chaining pipelines.

## Agent Guidance

- [Agent Operational Manual (AGENTS.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/AGENTS.md): Authoritative operational rules for AI agents: CLI execution semantics, parameter preflight, samplesheet rules, identity safety, status inspection, locking, chaining, replay, scientific assessment, and benign warning triage.
- [Claude Code Entry Point (CLAUDE.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/CLAUDE.md): Entry point for Anthropic Claude Code; it imports AGENTS.md rather than repeating it.

## Essential Documentation

- [Repository Overview & Quickstart (README.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/README.md): Repository layout, quickstart examples, provenance bundles, scientific validation notes, and citations.
- [System Architecture (docs/architecture.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/architecture.md): Four architectural zones, schema preflight gates, non-blocking sibling writer locks (`.nfclaw.lock`), cryptographic provenance bundles, and scientific assessment engine.
- [Pipeline Chaining Engine (docs/chaining.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/chaining.md): Multi-stage workflow orchestration, declarative JSON specs, cryptographic handoff verification, automated stage retries, and lineage tracking.
- [Engine Compatibility & Runtime Controls (docs/compatibility.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/compatibility.md): Nextflow DSL2 compatibility, Nextflow engine version pinning (`--nxf-ver`), JVM tuning (`--nxf-env`), and host resource limit controls (`--limit-*`).
- [Timeouts, Long Analyses & Monitoring (docs/timeouts.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/timeouts.md): Optional shared execution deadlines, configurable setup/shutdown margins, whole-controller background execution, and quick chain status without lineage verification.
- [Known Issues & Operational Troubleshooting (docs/known-issues.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/known-issues.md): Triage guide for benign upstream Nextflow warnings (e.g. nf-schema config scopes), host environment issues (IPv6, disk, permissions), and pipeline-specific workarounds.
- [Preflight Scope & Generation Matrix (docs/preflight.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/preflight.md): Wrapper validation scope, checked/deferred/unsupported rules, and the 95-pipeline samplesheet generation support matrix.
- [Scientific Output Contracts (docs/scientific-output-contracts.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/scientific-output-contracts.md): Specification for `nfclaw assess`: exact parsed format comparisons (BAM, VCF, FASTA, TSV, H5AD), sample coverage, and rational arithmetic tolerances.
- [Recorded Workflow Source Corrections (docs/source-corrections.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/source-corrections.md): Recorded, independently copied workflow corrections for Createtaxdb, Funcscan, and Bactmap, with source-bound replay.
- [Publication Evidence Policy (docs/maintenance.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/maintenance.md): Gated automated publication policy: candidate freezing, full matrix checks, raw task trace verification, and immutable artifact retention.
- [DRAMP Reference Preparation (docs/dramp-reference.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/dramp-reference.md): Preparation, validation, and container-indexed caching of DRAMP antimicrobial peptide references for Funcscan.
- [End-to-End Validation (docs/validation.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/validation.md): How every pinned pipeline and nfclaw's replay, resume, chain and stop handling were run end to end, how every pipeline's provenance bundle was replayed with its recorded container digests and execution environment, what passed, the settings each run needed, and the limits of that evidence.
- [MCP Server (docs/mcp.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/mcp.md): `nfclaw mcp` for Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Hermes and other MCP clients: per-client setup, the tools (each one an nfclaw command), detached restart-safe jobs for long runs and chains, served skills and docs, and the dual-era (2026-07-28 and handshake) protocol support.
- [Upstream Tracking & Maintenance Automation (docs/updating.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/updating.md): Submodule version tracking, automated release bumping, schema drift auditing (`librarian.check_drift`), and zero-drift policy.

## Pipeline Catalogs & Library

- [Pipeline Catalog Markdown (catalog.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/catalog.md): Human-readable index of every tracked nf-core pipeline with its pinned version, declared input, output locations and description (use grep; do not read whole).
- [Pipeline Catalog JSON (catalog.json)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/catalog.json): Machine-readable catalog: for every tracked pipeline its name, pinned version, description, summary, declared input, output locations, tools and the pipelines it feeds (use grep; do not read whole).
- [Upstream Sources Manifest (sources.tsv)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/sources.tsv): Tab-separated registry mapping each pipeline to its upstream Git repository and tracking policy.
- [Pipeline Library Directory (pipelines/)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/tree/main/pipelines): Library of individual pipelines (`pipelines/<name>/`), each holding pinned code (`upstream/`), agent instructions (`skill.md`), and complete parameter schemas (`reference.md`).

## Optional

- [Contributing Guidelines (CONTRIBUTING.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): Guide for contributing new pipelines, modifying librarian automation, and running tests.
- [Security Policy (SECURITY.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/SECURITY.md): How to report a suspected vulnerability privately, and what is in scope.
- [Live Web Portal](https://bmds-tue.github.io/nf-claw/): Interactive web portal for exploring pipelines, parameter schemas, live GitHub Actions workflows, and system architecture.
- [Academic Citation (CITATION.cff)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/CITATION.cff): Citation Metadata Format file for referencing nf-claw and wrapped nf-core pipelines.
